sections.title: A feeling, then the subjunctive
sections.content: You know *alegrar*, *molestar* and *sorprender* from A2 Unit 27: a feeling about something takes *que* + subjunctive (*Me alegra que estés aquí*). The thing you react to may be perfectly real, but you are reacting to it, not announcing it. This lesson only widens the range of reactions you can use. Unit 6 comes back to feelings in detail.

items.spanish: Me alegra que por fin tengas un trabajo nuevo.
items.english: I'm glad that you finally have a new job.

items.spanish: Lamento que no puedan venir a la cena.
items.english: I'm sorry that you cannot come to the dinner.

items.spanish: Me sorprende que Carmen no haya llegado todavía.
items.english: It surprises me that Carmen hasn't arrived yet.

items.spanish: Nos alegra que hayan encontrado una solución.
items.english: We are glad that they have found a solution.

sections.content: You know *haya* from B1 Unit 37 for a finished event: *Me sorprende que hayas venido*. After a past reaction, the imperfect: *Me alegró que vinieras*.
